newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates softer after fall in overnight.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates softer after fall in overnight.

text.p: Interbank rates were generally softer on Thursday but falls were limited by fresh borrowings, dealers said.
Swaps, meanwhile, moved to the right amid talk that Bank Negara will be holding a meeting with banks concerning the swaps, they said.
"I heard the meeting will be held either today or tomorrow. It's creating some uncertainty and pushing swaps to the right," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Bank Negara officials were not immediately available for confirmation.
The overnight rate fell to as low as 6.0 percent on Wednesday, triggered by rumours that the statutory reserve requirement (SRR) may be cut due to the current tight liquidity situation.
"The rumour is still in the market though many are beginning to rule out the possibility of such a move," said one dealer.
Dealers said a cut in the SRR -- funds that must be placed interest free with the central bank -- would send a wrong signal to the market as monetary and consumption growth were still high.
Talk of the SRR cut followed Bank Negara's move in providing liquidity for the market via one-month money this week.
One-, two- and three-week money were at 7.50/80 percent against 7.80/8.30 percent on Wednesday, dealers said.
One-month money was at 7.90/8.10 percent from 8.10/20, and three-month at 7.80/8.0 percent against 8.00/10.
The overnight was expected to trade between 7.0 and 8.0 percent on Thursday, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were down across the board.
At 0400 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down five points to 92.10, or an implied yield of 7.90 percent.
The September contract was down three at 92.44, or 7.56 percent, and December was also down three at 92.53, or 7.47 percent.
